overall: Los Angeles is starting July 5th under a strong marine layer influence, with temperatures stuck in the mid-64s°F since at least 03:52 ET and a velocity of effectively 0°F/hr — no meaningful warming has occurred this morning. The high dewpoint (~61°F) and patchy fog (expected to linger until ~11am per NWS) are suppressing early-day heating, a classic coastal marine pattern. Once the fog burns off the day should trend toward mostly sunny skies and afternoon warming into the low 70s.
forecast_obs_notes: Most NWP models cluster tightly around 71.6–73.5°F (ECMWF 71.6, HRRR 71.9, GFS 73.5), with NBM notably cooler at 69.3°F — likely capturing more marine layer persistence. The META (fused) model overwhelmingly favors the 72–73°F bucket at 77.8%, providing high confidence around the NWS call and overriding the NBM outlier.
